title: A longitude test finds no clear limb-specific fall in Locarno weighted spot counts near 1981
abstract: We test whether the Locarno count fall near 1981 has an extra loss away from the central meridian. We use 1,356 complete active drawings in November 1978 to June 1983. In the main model at matched F10.7, weighted counts fall by 13.84% in the central band and 13.58% in the outer band. The outer-to-central change is +0.30%, with a conditional 95% interval from -9.02% to +10.73%. Mg II gives +0.77% (-9.13% to +11.26%). Neither reference shows a clear extra outer loss. Longitude cuts and seeing controls retain the central radio fall. A single-observer flat model includes no central change. Time slopes change the estimates. The archive changes from software to manual positions at the boundary; radial two-degree shifts change the ratio estimate by about ten percentage points. The result limits a limb-only loss under the main model. It does not distinguish a physical spot-size change from counting practice or prove equal longitude responses. Code, model estimates, figure, source hashes and external-data retrieval instructions are included. External observations stay outside the publication.

display.caption: Fitted January 1981 changes in central and outer longitude bands at matched emission. Intervals are conditional 95% residual block-bootstrap intervals. Flat and separate time-slope models share the same observations. W is weighted spot count, not measured area.
